To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the number of measurements needed for support recovery scales linearly with the number of nonzero coefficients, (ii) for linear models, the number of measurements scales with the number of nonzeros plus the number of nonzero rows, (iii) for 1-bit models, the number scales with the number nonzeros, and (iv) for group testing models, the number also scales with the number nonzero rows.

for a general probabilistic model relating a sparse data signal to observations, we characterize the information-theoretically necessary and sufficient number (and constant factors) of measurements to recover the support of the data signal exactly, and we also provide a general converse bound for partial support recovery.

for the linear model with a Gaussian measurement matrix, the necessary and sufficient minimum number of measurements is Θ(k log(n/k)) and the corresponding error probability is Θ(e−k log(n/k)), and for the 1-bit model with a Gaussian random measurement matrix, the error probability tends to one if the measurement vector is not sufficiently sparse.
